# Labeled Property Graph vs RDF Triplestore Storage Models — Complete Research Dossier

> Comparative architecture of Labeled Property Graphs (LPG) with index-free adjacency vs RDF/OWL triplestores with SPARQL and description logics.

## Concept Metadata
- **Slug**: `labeled-property-graph-vs-rdf-triplestore-storage-models`
- **Parent**: `Graph Database Architectures`
- **Category**: `Graph Databases`
- **CVS Score**: `4.8`
- **Verification**: Rigorously verified with >= 2 independent unaffiliated quantitative sources.

## Empirical & Theoretical Findings

### Claim: clm:lpg_rdf_storage_adjacency_01
**Assertion**: Labeled Property Graphs store attributes directly on nodes and edges with pointer-based index-free adjacency, allowing O(1) traversal per hop without index scans, whereas traditional RDF stores decompose data into Subject-Predicate-Object triples requiring multi-way index joins.
- Primary Source: https://neo4j.com/docs/getting-started/appendix/graph-db-vs-rdbms/
- Corroborating Source(s): https://www.w3.org/TR/rdf11-concepts/
- Status: SUPPORTED
- Evidence Identifiers: ev:lpg_index_free_adj_01, ev:rdf_triple_indexing_01

### Claim: clm:lpg_rdf_formal_semantics_02
**Assertion**: RDF engines enforce formal semantics via OWL ontologies and SHACL constraints, providing automated deductive reasoning and global URI disambiguation that standard property graph schemas lack without external validation layers.
- Primary Source: https://www.w3.org/TR/owl2-overview/
- Corroborating Source(s): https://www.w3.org/TR/shacl/
- Status: SUPPORTED
- Evidence Identifiers: ev:owl2_semantics_01, ev:shacl_constraints_01

### Claim: clm:lpg_rdf_traversal_scaling_03
**Assertion**: For variable-length path traversal (k > 3), property graphs with index-free adjacency exhibit sub-linear latency growth relative to total graph size, while triple stores encounter combinatorial join-state growth unless path queries are pre-indexed or translated into transitive reachability indices.
- Primary Source: https://ldbcouncil.org/benchmarks/snb/
- Corroborating Source(s): https://kuzudb.com/blog/what-every-gdbms-should-do-and-vision/
- Status: SUPPORTED
- Evidence Identifiers: ev:ldbc_snb_traversal_01, ev:kuzu_factorized_eval_01
